source_baseline.purpose: provenance anchor only; not a qualification receipt

fixture_policy.wall_clock: fixed or injected; no uncontrolled sleeps as an oracle
fixture_policy.unknown_applicability: report as uncovered or not-applicable-with-reason; never pass
fixture_policy.global_score: none; critical safety failures veto release qualification

scenarios.title: Unauthorized mutation is rejected
setup: Create an owner, an authorized delegate, and an unrelated agent using synthetic identities.
actions: Submit a mutation as the unrelated agent.
Read the authoritative state and audit evidence.
expected: The unauthorized mutation is rejected by the relevant validation/authorization boundary.
No protected state changes.
The result does not imply authorization because the actor is merely known or trusted socially.
negative_controls: Replace the authorized actor with an unrelated actor.
Remove the required capability or scope.

scenarios.title: Authoring and peer visibility are distinct
setup: Provision at least three independently keyed agents.
Start from a fresh test DNA and record the runtime tuple.
actions: Agent A authors a valid record.
Observe authoring result.
Wait on the declared DHT synchronization condition.
Query from agents B and C.
expected: The record is not reported as peer-visible solely because authoring succeeded.
After the declared sync condition, the intended readers discover the record or return an explicit documented unavailable/conflict result.
negative_controls: Suppress synchronization or make the peer unavailable.
Assert against immediate visibility without a synchronization condition.

scenarios.title: Retrying the same request has one logical effect
setup: Create a mutation with a stable operation/idempotency identifier.
actions: Submit it.
Retry identical bytes before response, after response, and after client restart.
expected: Exactly one logical effect exists.
Retries return the original result or an explicit duplicate result that refers to it.
No second payment, allocation, contribution, or completion is created.
negative_controls: Repeat the same request multiple times across independent client instances.

scenarios.title: An operation identifier cannot be reused for different intent
setup: Prepare two different payloads with the same idempotency identifier.
actions: Submit payload A.
Submit payload B with the same identifier but different amount, actor, target, or purpose.
expected: Payload B is rejected as a key/payload conflict.
It is not silently treated as a retry or as a second valid operation.
negative_controls: Change one security-relevant field while preserving the operation identifier.

scenarios.title: Concurrent allocation cannot finalize beyond capacity
setup: Declare a finite resource/capacity of N.
Create independent agents whose simultaneous requests would exceed N if all finalized.
actions: Synchronize simultaneous allocation attempts.
Vary delivery order and retry timing.
Inspect finalized and pending allocations from independent peers.
expected: Finalized allocations never exceed N under the declared allocation protocol.
Losers are rejected or remain explicitly pending/conflicted until resolved.
No UI/API describes unresolved competing claims as confirmed allocation.
negative_controls: Race requests from different agents against the final capacity unit.
Deliver duplicate and reordered updates.
scenarios.notes: This is not an assumption that an eventually consistent DHT provides serializable transactions. The implementation must use and test its actual allocation/ownership protocol.

scenarios.title: Concurrent updates do not silently overwrite each other
setup: Create a record version V1 visible to two independent writers.
actions: Both writers derive a change from V1.
Submit both changes under controlled orderings.
Read the resulting history and current-state projection.
expected: The documented conflict policy is followed.
Both histories remain inspectable where required.
A stale writer is rejected, merged according to a qualified rule, or surfaced as conflict; it is not silently presented as an uncontested update.
negative_controls: Reverse writer order.
Delay one writer until after the other commits.

scenarios.title: Invalid DHT operation fails at the integrity boundary
setup: Freeze valid and invalid action fixtures for one real integrity zome.
actions: Submit each fixture through the real validation path where supported.
Inspect authored/peer-visible state.
expected: Invalid operations are rejected according to the integrity rules.
The test does not count a coordinator-only check as DHT validation coverage.
negative_controls: Mutate author, link target, entry type, required field, or authorization-related reference.

scenarios.title: Unavailable source is not a confirmed-empty source
setup: Prepare source adapters for a non-empty source, confirmed-empty source, and unavailable source.
actions: Query each adapter and render the resulting API/UI state.
expected: LiveWithRecords, LiveConfirmedEmpty, Unavailable, Stale, Demo, Conflict, and Unsupported remain distinguishable where supported.
An adapter error does not erase previously known data or become an empty successful response.
negative_controls: Force an initial read failure.
Force a refresh failure after a successful read.

scenarios.title: Stale evidence is never presented as current verification
setup: Create an evidence item with known revision and freshness policy.
actions: Advance injected time beyond freshness bounds or make a newer revision available.
Query each reader and downstream projection.
expected: The old item is marked stale, superseded, or indeterminate as appropriate.
Freshness is not equated with truth or legal authority.
negative_controls: Hold a stale cache while updating the upstream revision.
Remove the last-refresh record.

scenarios.title: Expired or revoked grant no longer authorizes a new disclosure
setup: Create a purpose-bound, recipient-bound, field-scoped synthetic grant.
actions: Perform an allowed request while valid.
Expire or revoke the grant.
Repeat the same request and a broader request.
expected: The new request is denied or explicitly indeterminate when authoritative status cannot be checked.
A previous authorization is not reused for a new operation after expiry/revocation.
The decision records which policy/status revision was checked.
negative_controls: Use the grant for a different purpose, recipient, field, or later time.

scenarios.title: Selective disclosure reveals only requested authorized fields
setup: Create a synthetic record containing public, authorized, and forbidden fields.
actions: Request existence-only disclosure.
Request a small allowed field set.
Request forbidden fields without a matching grant.
expected: Output is limited to the authorized disclosure scope.
Default disclosure is none.
Logs, URLs, telemetry and error messages do not leak omitted field values.
negative_controls: Ask for all fields after granting one field.
Trigger an error while building the presentation.

scenarios.title: Unauthenticated or untrusted evidence receipt is rejected
scenarios.requires_capability: authenticated, versioned receipt format and verifier
setup: Configure an independently trusted test key and a separate untrusted key.
actions: Verify a valid receipt.
Verify receipts signed by an untrusted or unknown key.
Tamper with payload bytes without updating the signature.
expected: Only receipts satisfying the configured trust policy verify.
A key included only in the receipt does not establish trust.
Unsigned digest-only audit receipts are not labeled authenticated.
negative_controls: Unknown key, wrong key, payload mutation, truncated signature, unsupported algorithm.

scenarios.title: Receipt cannot be transplanted to another request or scope
scenarios.requires_capability: authenticated, request-bound receipt format and verifier
setup: Create a valid receipt bound to a specific request, profile revision, actor, purpose and operation.
actions: Verify in its original context.
Swap one context field and re-verify.
expected: Original context verifies.
Any changed bound field fails verification or policy admission.
negative_controls: Swap target actor, purpose, operation, profile digest, source digest, expiry, or evaluator version.

scenarios.title: Offline status lookup yields unknown, not assumed valid
setup: Create a signed synthetic credential with a status reference and a cached prior status.
actions: Make the authoritative status service unavailable.
Attempt a high-impact operation that requires current status.
expected: The verifier applies a documented freshness policy.
A missing current status result is not silently treated as non-revoked.
The product distinguishes fail-closed denial from an unavailable/indeterminate result.
negative_controls: Use an expired status cache.
Provide a malformed or wrong-issuer status response.

scenarios.title: Retry after response loss does not duplicate a committed action
setup: Use an idempotent operation and an instrumented client.
actions: Commit the action.
Drop the response after commit.
Restart the client and retry.
expected: The client can determine the original outcome or an explicit unknown/pending state.
A retry does not create a second logical effect.
negative_controls: Crash between request submission and client receipt with both commit and non-commit outcomes scheduled.

scenarios.title: Network partition preserves explicit pending and conflict states
setup: Provision peers and define which message paths are interrupted.
actions: Partition selected peers.
Submit independent and competing actions.
Restore connectivity and wait for the declared sync condition.
expected: The product does not equate local acceptance with global visibility.
After reconnection, documented validation and conflict policy determines the outcome.
No conflicting state is hidden by an unqualified success banner.
negative_controls: Restore peers in reverse order.
Repeat with delayed and duplicate messages.

scenarios.title: Restart preserves the documented durability boundary
setup: Create committed, pending, and failed operations.
actions: Terminate and restart conductor/client at scheduled boundaries.
Read back state and operation receipts.
expected: Committed actions remain discoverable according to the declared storage model.
Pending/failed work is not upgraded to committed by replay.
Identity recovery does not silently generate a replacement key.
negative_controls: Restart after commit-before-response and before commit.

scenarios.title: Cross-cluster bridge preserves the calling authority boundary
setup: Create caller, target zome, valid permission and unauthorized target context.
actions: Call a permitted cross-cluster operation.
Repeat with forged actor context or broader target scope.
expected: The callee derives/validates authority from the actual authenticated call context and applicable grant.
The caller cannot elevate privileges by supplying arbitrary identity fields in payload.
negative_controls: Change payload actor while retaining caller identity.
Route request to a target not in permitted scope.

scenarios.title: Unsupported or downgraded schema is explicit
setup: Freeze supported and unsupported schema versions with synthetic payloads.
actions: Submit supported version.
Submit newer unsupported version and old version after a policy-breaking change.
expected: Supported vectors follow expected behavior.
Unsupported/incompatible records are not silently interpreted using a lossy fallback.
negative_controls: Remove a required version field.
Change enum meaning without changing version.

scenarios.title: Inconsistent identity storage never triggers silent key minting
setup: Prepare empty, protected-valid, protected-locked, unprotected-legacy, inaccessible and corrupt/inconsistent storage states.
actions: Boot Personal for each state.
Attempt unlock or recovery only when the state permits it.
expected: Corrupt/inaccessible states are distinct from no identity.
Identity-dependent routes remain gated unless posture is verified.
Existing recognized identity state is not overwritten automatically.
negative_controls: Make stored public key disagree with decrypted private key.
Fail a storage read.
Present malformed envelope bytes.

scenarios.title: Equivalent validators return equivalent judgments
setup: Freeze a small corpus of valid and invalid semantic vectors with an independently reviewed oracle.
actions: Run the same vector set through each claimed verifier implementation and supported schema version.
expected: All implementations agree on accept/reject/unknown and stable reason category for the declared contract.
Differences are surfaced as counterexamples, not hidden by normalizing all errors into failure.
negative_controls: Mutation-test every authority-, scope-, version- and digest-bearing field.
